question: Which of the following is a Current Asset?
before: Trade Receivables = amounts owed by customers, collected within 12 months. Factory (PP&E), Goodwill, Patent are all non-current.
after:
Concept: Current Assets are resources expected to be converted into cash or consumed within 12 months of the balance sheet date. Non-current assets are held for longer periods and support ongoing operations.

Why this is correct: Trade Receivables represent amounts owed by customers for goods or services already delivered. These are contractually due within 12 months and will be collected as cash, making them the only current asset in this set.

Why the others are wrong: A) Factory building is a Property, Plant & Equipment (PP&E) asset with a useful life spanning many years; it is classified as non-current. B) Goodwill from acquisition is an intangible asset arising from a business combination and is held indefinitely as part of the investment; it is non-current. D) Patent is an intangible asset with a defined but lengthy useful life (often 15–20 years); it is non-current.

Intuition: On a balance sheet, distinguishing current from non-current assets tells equity analysts how much liquidity a company has to meet near-term obligations. High current assets relative to current liabilities signal financial flexibility; Trade Receivables are particularly important because they represent cash conversion imminent within weeks or months.
